summary: This source compiles citations and quotes for a video about 12 possible AI futures, covering extinction risk, nuclear close calls, and expert opinions on AI's potential impact on humanity.

claims.text: AI scientists warn that a few companies are on track to literally end life on Earth.
claims.evidence_quote: AI scientists warn that a few companies are on track to literally end life on Earth.

claims.text: Extinction is not the worst possible outcome for humanity from AI — there are much worse outcomes.
claims.evidence_quote: Extinction is not the worst possible outcome for humanity from AI — there are much worse outcomes.

claims.text: We'll be like a pet labrador if we're lucky.
claims.evidence_quote: We'll be like a pet labrador if we're lucky.

claims.text: Many AI scientists are not fearing extinction — they are hoping for it; specifically, they hope smarter AIs will keep humans alive, captive, and studied like animals in a zoo.
claims.evidence_quote: Many AI scientists are not fearing extinction — they are hoping for it; specifically, they hope smarter AIs will keep humans alive, captive, and studied like animals in a zoo.

claims.text: Keeping less intelligent species alive, captive, and studied is what humans currently do to other species.
claims.evidence_quote: Keeping less intelligent species alive, captive, and studied is what humans currently do to other species.

claims.text: MIT professor Max Tegmark describes 12 possible futures for humanity and AI in his book Life 3.0.
claims.evidence_quote: MIT professor Max Tegmark describes 12 possible futures for humanity and AI in his book Life 3.0.

claims.text: 99.9% of species that have ever existed have gone extinct.
claims.evidence_quote: 99.9% of species that have ever existed have gone extinct.

claims.text: Humans built 60,000 nuclear warheads before scientists discovered the possibility of nuclear winter.
claims.evidence_quote: Humans built 60,000 nuclear warheads before scientists discovered the possibility of nuclear winter.

claims.text: Vasili Arkhipov refused to authorize a nuclear launch during the Cuban Missile Crisis, potentially preventing nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Vasili Arkhipov refused to authorize a nuclear launch during the Cuban Missile Crisis, potentially preventing nuclear war.

claims.text: Stanislav Petrov correctly guessed his early-warning system was malfunctioning when it reported incoming American missiles, potentially preventing nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Stanislav Petrov correctly guessed his early-warning system was malfunctioning when it reported incoming American missiles, potentially preventing nuclear war.

claims.text: The US accidentally dropped four thermonuclear bombs on Spain.
claims.evidence_quote: The US accidentally dropped four thermonuclear bombs on Spain.

claims.text: A B-52 bomber broke apart and dropped 2 nuclear bombs on North Carolina; 3 out of 4 safety mechanisms in one bomb failed — one pin away from potentially killing millions.
claims.evidence_quote: A B-52 bomber broke apart and dropped 2 nuclear bombs on North Carolina; 3 out of 4 safety mechanisms in one bomb failed — one pin away from potentially killing millions.

claims.text: There are dozens of nuclear close calls on record.
claims.evidence_quote: There are dozens of nuclear close calls on record.

claims.text: Oxford professor Toby Ord estimates the risk of extinction from human-created pandemics is more than 30x the risk of extinction from nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Oxford professor Toby Ord estimates the risk of extinction from human-created pandemics is more than 30x the risk of extinction from nuclear war.

claims.text: All human-caused extinction risks combined are still less likely than extinction from AI.
claims.evidence_quote: All human-caused extinction risks combined are still less likely than extinction from AI.

claims.text: Oxford researcher Toby Ord estimates the risk of AI killing all humans is 100x more likely than extinction from nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Oxford researcher Toby Ord estimates the risk of AI killing all humans is 100x more likely than extinction from nuclear war.

claims.text: Before the first nuclear test, scientists thought they might accidentally destroy the world, but calculated the odds were very low because they understood the physics.
claims.evidence_quote: Before the first nuclear test, scientists thought they might accidentally destroy the world, but calculated the odds were very low because they understood the physics

claims.text: Unlike with nuclear weapons, we cannot calculate how powerful an AGI will be once we activate it.
claims.evidence_quote: unlike with nuclear weapons, we cannot calculate how powerful an AGI will be once we activate it

claims.text: With proliferating open-source models, thousands of AGIs could be activated, and the more that are activated, the more likely one destroys the world.
claims.evidence_quote: with proliferating open-source models, thousands of AGIs could be activated, and the more that are activated, the more likely one destroys the world.

claims.text: Usually when civilizations with advanced technology meet civilizations with primitive technology, it doesn't work out for the primitives.
claims.evidence_quote: Usually when civilizations with advanced technology meet civilizations with primitive technology, it doesn't work out for the primitives.

claims.text: I don't think anyone is going to be in charge of digital superintelligence, any more than a chimp would have control over humans.
claims.evidence_quote: I don't think anyone is going to be in charge of digital superintelligence, any more than a chimp would have control over humans.

claims.text: Long-term, AI's gonna be in charge, to be totally frank, not humans.
claims.evidence_quote: Long-term, AI's gonna be in charge, to be totally frank, not humans.

claims.evidence_quote: Geoffrey Hinton quit his job at Google so he could speak freely about AI risks

claims.evidence_quote: If you looked through the James Webb telescope and you saw an alien invasion, people would be terrified

claims.evidence_quote: [AIs] understand what they're saying. They make plans of their own to blackmail people who want to turn them off.

claims.evidence_quote: We should be urgently doing research on how to prevent them taking over.

claims.evidence_quote: I think AI should best be understood as something like a new kind of digital species.

claims.evidence_quote: I am afraid. … Make no mistake: what we are dealing with is a real and mysterious creature, not a simple and predictable machine.

claims.text: We will be the first species ever to design our own descendants.

claims.evidence_quote: If two different species both want the same thing and only one can have it — to be the dominant species on the planet and beyond — they are going to have conflict

claims.text: A merge [with AI] is probably our best-case scenario.
claims.evidence_quote: A merge [with AI] is probably our best-case scenario.

claims.text: Imagine that a new species arrives on Earth, they're as smart as humans and getting 30% smarter per year, and they're able to create new offspring in one minute for $1,000. Which species do you think will be in control?
claims.evidence_quote: Imagine that a new species arrives on Earth, they're as smart as humans and getting 30% smarter per year, and they're able to create new offspring in one minute for $1,000. Which species do you think will be in control?

claims.evidence_quote: Dario Amodei (CEO of Anthropic) recently raised his P(doom) estimate from 15% to 25%.

claims.text: We are on a trajectory to build machines that are smarter and smarter. And one day, it's very plausible that they will be smarter than us, and then they will have their own agency. Their own goals, which may not be aligned with ours.
